messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: constraints & renamed cmd options
parts:
I just committed a major patch to the way
variable constraints work in Stan (for everything
but parameters).

1. All variables allow constraints other than
local variables.

2. Data and transformed data constraints are enforced
after data is read in.

3. Transformed parameters checked as sample is written.

4. Generated quantities checked as sample is written.

5. Testing constraints is done through cassert (at least
for now) and can be turned off for extra speed like
other asserts during compilation.

I also changed the names of command-line parameters.
These are now available from the compiled command via
--help, which now prints:

~/stan>demo/temp --help

Compiled Stan Graphical Model Command

USAGE: demo/temp [options]

OPTIONS:

--help Display this information

--data=<file> Read data from specified dump-format file
(required if model declares data)

--seed=<int> Set random number generation seed

--inits=<file> Use initial values from specialized file
(default is random initialization)

--iter=<+int> Total number of iterations, including burn in
(default = 2000)

--burnin=<+int> Discard the specified number of initial samples
(default = iter / 2)

--thin=<+int> Period between saved samples after burn in
(default = max(1, floor(iter - burnin) / 1000))

--delta=<+float> Initial parameter for NUTS step-size tuning.
(default = 0.5)

--samples=<file> File into which samples are written.
(default = samples.csv)

--append_samples Append samples to existing samples file if it exists
(default erases existing samples file before
writing)

--refresh=<+int> Period between samples producing progress output
(default = max(1,iter/200))
- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: constraints & renamed cmd options
parts:
Some issues with these command options. First, --seed is currently
allowed to be a string, which causes the seed to be 0, which
nonetheless says is "randomly generated". My guess is that this is due
to the "characters are ints" paradigm of C-based languages and
afflicts many of the options. E.g.

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan-svn$ demo/ds --data=/opt/wawro/third/
ds.dump --iter=4 --seed="foobar"
NUTS
sample_file=samples.csv
num_iterations=4
num_burnin=2
num_thin=1
delta=0.5
random seed=0 (randomly generated)
iteration=1 burning in
iteration=2 burning in
iteration=3 saving
iteration=4 saving

Also, I think if a --seed is supplied by the user, it should say
random seed = X (user supplied) rather than random seed = X (randomly
generated).

Can we make it so that if --refresh is 0, then it doesn't print
anything to stdout? Also, no matter what you set --refresh to
currently, it prints every iteration.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: constraints & renamed cmd options
parts:
All good suggestions. Thanks for looking so
closely and kicking the tires. (I should've
mentioned that the options weren't all implemented
yet, even in theory, like pruning the updating
printing -- I'm not even sure thinning is implemented
on the inside, but these are all trivial to do.)

I'm also going to work on a number of chains arg
for Andrew and in that, I'll take a single seed
and generate the seeds for the other chains by
advancing the random number generator.

I'm working on my meetup talk now, so I won't have
time to do this (or change beta to lbeta) until
tomorrow.

- Bob
